acceptance.criterion: Specify the independent failure domain, ordered policy events/checkpoints, authenticity and completeness checks, and the trusted recovery authority.

Define the commit/acknowledgment protocol for grants, revocations, disablement and stewardship changes, including every crash/replication-failure window; no acknowledged restrictive change can disappear on restore.
Define closed-service behavior when currency cannot be proved and distinguish scientific-data RPO from policy/lifecycle durability.

observed.rejectedAlternative: local commit/ack then async replication can resurrect a revoked grant after primary loss
observed.review: engineering adversarial review before persistence work; trust/fencing assumptions and unresolved-intent availability cost explicit

handoff.F02.2: single principal registry, transactional organization policy revision/event/receipt; local-only durability must be explicit; fence legacy recovery
handoff.F03.2: join policy lock, current authorization and event/receipt in same transaction
handoff.O03.2: implement independent PREPARE/COMMIT/ABORT witness, current challenge/barrier, key and epoch custody, and real fault matrix

limits: Finite abstract protocol model, not a proof over unbounded histories.
HMAC models authenticity only; Ed25519/TLS/keys and real durable I/O remain O03.2.
External writer fencing and non-rollback witness continuity are explicit assumptions, not inferred from signatures.
No deployed independent recovery or institutional physical-loss qualification.
No institution/operator approval inferred; actual independent medium and approvers remain O03.3/SITE01.
Unresolved intent after primary loss keeps recovery unavailable until a separately reviewed resolution protocol exists.
